$comment: Round 18 lane L7 (INSTRUMENT RED-TEAM) ledger fragment. Entries whose id starts with RESTATE- do NOT change an existing entry's verdict; they narrow the stated SCOPE of an existing negative, in the sense of AGENTS.md section 7 (trust the bound, distrust the conclusion). Merge into liber-primus/LEDGER.json.
trust_anchor: tests/validate.py ALL PASS (5/5 known solves); benchmark/gates.py 7/7

entries.hypothesis: Every adjudication in this repository is decided by lp.score.Quadgram.score_norm, a quadgram model trained on four modern-orthography English books, against a fixed English band (>= -5.5). If the LP2 plaintext is not modern or archaic English, the CORRECT key is scored as noise and every published negative is conditional in a way no ledger entry states.
entries.coverage: Measured the correct-key beam score for 10 plaintext registers x 4 segment lengths (31/120/240/400) x 12 replicates, under the pinned soft anti-repeat filter with the sha256_ctr(CICADA3301) key family. Instrument unchanged from the repo. Recovery measured on rune indices.
not_covered: languages not modelled (Greek, Hebrew, Norse, Enochian, constructed languages)
non-linguistic payloads (key blocks, hashes, base32) - B6 proved these undetectable in principle
the matched runic scorer of round16/scorer, which no lane has yet adopted
key families other than sha256_ctr (the effect is a property of the scorer, not the key, but only one family was measured)
entries.threshold: A register is INVISIBLE if its median correct-key score_norm < -5.5 (the repo-wide bar). Fixed in PREREG.md before running. FOUND-ERROR iff >= 1 plausible register is INVISIBLE at L=120 or L=400 and no ledger entry states the English conditionality.

result.median_rune_index_recovery_of_the_correc: 100% for LATIN, OE, DE, CY and EN_HALFVOWEL at every length. The DECODER recovers the plaintext exactly; only the ADJUDICATOR fails.
result.EN_NOVOWEL_is_anti_selected: correct key -7.597 vs a deliberately wrong key -7.405: an abbreviated-English plaintext ranks the correct key BELOW a wrong one.
result.word_boundary_free_is_a_non_issue: the quadgram model is built with [^A-Z] stripped (data/BUILD-QUADGRAMS.md), so it is already matched to boundary-free rune output.
result.no_ledger_entry_states_the_condition: the word 'English' appears in no coverage or not_covered field of the 62 LEDGER.json entries.

entries.reopens_if: n/a - this is an instrument measurement, not an attack lane. It is superseded when a lane adopts a non-English or language-agnostic adjudicator and re-reports its power.

entries.coverage: 340 archived candidate decode strings - every top50/top20 'head' field in round13/B04 A-D, round16/KDF, round16/prng and round17 P0-P3 - re-scored under rune-space trigram LMs for EN/LA/OE/DE/CY/the real LP1 register plus decrypt-IoC.N.

Round 8's 2.52e9 decodes, which stored no candidate strings at all
registers whose correct key would not have entered a top-N in the first place (Welsh, vowel-dropped English) - see the power field

entries.threshold: B6's rule verbatim: z >= 4.0 against a length-matched 400-sample random-rune null AND above that null's maximum. Because every archived candidate is the ENGLISH argmax of its sweep, the selection-corrected statistic score_M - score_EN, standardised against the archive's own distribution, is reported as the operative one.

result.raw_flags_are_selection_artifact: English-correlated models (OE, DE) light up because the candidates were chosen as the English argmax

measured_power.LATIN: correct key would rank 1 of 1,385,600 (z=+7.6) and WOULD be stored -> the negative extends to Latin
measured_power.EN_NOVOWEL: expected rank 1.2e6 of 1.39e6 (z=-1.10) -> ZERO power, permanent blind spot of the archive

The 6,224,300 + 692,064 + 52,556 decodes and the ~14.5e9 offsets are adjudicated English-only and CANNOT be retro-fitted: only the argmax-by-English survivors still exist.

entries.hypothesis: skipdecode.beam_decode admits a key skip only if EVERY skipped key position would have reproduced the previous cipher rune. That validity test is exact for encipher_keyskip and for nothing else, so constructions that desynchronise the key for any other reason are excluded by the decoder's transition relation rather than merely being harder for it.
entries.coverage: 67 constructions x 7 seeds at L=240, English plaintext held fixed so the scorer is at full power. Axes: suppression 0.0-1.0; filter placement (key-skip / value-rewrite / key-side / plaintext-side); position-varying suppression (ramp, per-page blocks, burst); free key drift q=0-0.05; exactly n unrepresentable key advances n=0-10; rejection consuming two draws; low-entropy pads with constant runs r=1-32; max_skip 1-8; beam width 50-1000.
not_covered: unknown key offset (that is lane L6/B-02)
constructions combining two or more of these axes
plaintext registers other than English (that is sub-attack A)
entries.positive_control: passed - keyskip supp=0.83 max_skip=3 beam_w=400 recovers at -4.303, 100% rune recovery, reproducing the published gate
entries.threshold: A construction is MISSED iff the median correct-key score_norm over the seeds is < -5.5. FOUND-ERROR iff a MISSED construction also reproduces LP2's 0.664% doublet rate to within +-0.3pp and appears in no ledger not_covered field. Fixed in PREREG.md before running.

missed_and_LP2_doublet_consistent_and_un.construction: exactly 5 unrepresentable key advances per 240 runes

result.budget_is_not_the_binding_constraint: raising max_skip 3->8 and beam width 400->1000 changes these scores by exactly 0.000; the failure is in the transition relation, not the search depth
result.robust_axes: suppression 0.0-1.0, position-varying suppression (all three shapes), beam width 50-1000 and max_skip 1-8 on a high-entropy pad: correct key recovered at -4.30 / 100% throughout
result.max_skip_correction_extends_round17: R17 reported ms=3 underpowered on constant-byte runs and ms=8 as the fix. Measured here: at a hard filter (supp=1.0) ms=8 still FAILS at run length 16 (-6.503) and 32 (-7.054). The honest statement is 'ms=8 covers constant runs up to length 8'.
result.mechanism_placement_newly_excluded_by_th: a key-side filter (doublet-free keystream, rigid encipherment) yields a 3.77% ciphertext doublet rate and a plaintext-side filter yields 3.80%, against LP2's 0.664%. Only output-side placements (key-skip 0.84%, value-rewrite 0.42%) reproduce the observed statistic, and the beam handles both. The repo asserted this; it is now measured.

entries.reopens_if: n/a for the measurement. The constructions it names reopen the lanes that used the beam: any evidence that the 2013 rejection loop consumed more than one draw per rejection, or that an interrupter / line break / discarded draw advanced the key independently of the doublet rule, invalidates every beam-based negative in the repository.

entries.hypothesis: A load-bearing headline statistic is miscounted (a second, independent re-derivation of R12-D2 with fresh code).
entries.coverage: n, doublet count and rate, IoC*N, entropy and lag-1 suppression, recomputed from the pinned runes with independently written code.
entries.threshold: Independent recomputation must match the published value.

result.methodological_note: Lag-1 suppression is 1 - observed/expected where expected is the stream's OWN unigram collision rate (3.4478%), not 1/29 (3.4483%). They coincide here only because IoC*N = 1.0000.

entries.reopens_if: A transcription change (A-03) that alters n or the doublet count.

entries.hypothesis: The G3 doublet-deficit floor - min_d Pdp(d) > 0.664% for real plaintexts, therefore the key must be output-aware - is measured on four MODERN ENGLISH corpora only, and is English-conditional in the same way the scorer is.
entries.verdict: NO-ERROR-FOUND; the published bound is EXTENDED rather than corrected
entries.coverage: min_d Pdp(d) recomputed for the four published corpora, then computed for the first time on Latin, Old English, German, Welsh, the real LP1 solved-page register, half-vowel English and vowel-dropped English.
not_covered: Greek, Hebrew, Norse and constructed languages
non-linguistic plaintexts, which by construction can reach any floor
entries.threshold: Pre-registered: the G3 step is English-conditional if any register has min_d Pdp(d) <= 0.80% (the observed 0.664% plus ~2 SE at 86 doublets).

result.verdict: the G3 argument HOLDS across 9 registers in 5 languages including abbreviated forms
corrections_of_record: the floor's MARGIN is 1.46x (German), not the 2.26x implied by the quoted 1.50%
ELIMINATION-LEDGER.md:779 and round10/SYNTHESIS.md:74 still quote 'floor 1.50% (KJV)'; KJV's actual value is 1.386% and R12-D2 already superseded the figure with 1.38-1.83%

entries.reopens_if: A plausible plaintext register with min_d Pdp(d) <= 0.80%.

entries.hypothesis: benchmark/null.py's threshold_for() is a validated bar wherever the repo has used it.
entries.coverage: Re-derivation of DEFAULT_MU/DEFAULT_BETA from their two anchors; sampling-error propagation; out-of-sample residuals against all 9 recorded sweep maxima in the repo; direct measurement of mu and beta at (L, beam_w) = (31,120), (120,400), (400,120) with 400-sample shuffle nulls.
not_covered: decoders other than the skip-aware beam
entries.positive_control: the estimator reproduces the repo's own calibrated beta ratio structure; the 1/sqrt(L) law is confirmed (measured 2.00 vs predicted 1.97)
entries.threshold: Pre-registered: a residual > 3 Gumbel SD at any lane means the constants do not transfer there; a beta differing from DEFAULT_BETA by more than a factor 1.5 at L=400 means every threshold_for() value R17 reported is mis-calibrated.

result.circularity: both anchors are B-04's own order statistics, and threshold_for() was then used to adjudicate B-04
result.cause: R17 fed threshold_for() the number of OFFSETS SCANNED, but the adjudicated statistic is the maximum over the number of BEAM DECODES performed - lib_padsweep.escalate beam-decodes only the top 40 per (pad, builder, sign) prefilter survivors, i.e. ~1e3 not ~3e9. Inverting the model on the observed maxima gives an effective trial count of ~4e2.
result.evidence_in_R17s_own_file: round17/P1_blockchain/results.json records expected_null_max_at_n = -5.684 next to null_max_over_lane_ms8 = -6.822 and never reconciles the 1.14 gap
result.concrete_consequence: R17's headline P3 best of -5.679 was scored on a 31-rune head window. A 400-draw order-destroying shuffle null at L=31 reached -5.681 in this lane's measurement. A fixed -5.5 bar is not a bar at 31 runes, and the SYNTHESIS sentence presenting -5.679 as 0.18 short of a hit compares a 31-rune score to a bar calibrated on 120-400-rune segments.
result.no_verdict_flips: every best score in the repo is below both the reported and the corrected bar; the error is in the bar-independence argument, not in any NEGATIVE

entries.reopens_if: n/a - discharged when threshold_for() takes a segment length and lanes pass the number of decodes actually adjudicated rather than the number of offsets scanned.

entries.hypothesis: RECON-B item B-17: the multiple-comparisons tally is frozen at 5 across Rounds 8-9.
entries.verdict: FOUND-ERROR (recomputed; 5 was never right at any level of granularity)
entries.coverage: Recomputed at three levels over every round to date: pre-registered hypotheses, ledger entries, and decodes/offsets scored.
entries.threshold: The tally must be reported at a stated level of granularity with the family-wise bar it implies.

result.consequence: -5.5 is NOT the repo-wide bar; the decode-level family-wise bar is stricter at -5.210. No published verdict flips - every best score in the repo is below both.
result.caveat: these are not independent tests (the same 12,956 runes are re-decoded), so the union correction is conservative, which is the safe direction for a negative

entries.reopens_if: n/a - discharged when each round states which family it is controlling and reports the bar that family implies.

entries.was: Round 8 used a fixed bar; round10/L5-seed32 later proved that bar is STATISTICALLY INVALID at full-32 scale.
entries.restated_coverage: Quantified: threshold_for() crosses the -5.5 floor at N* = 3.13e8. Round 8's 2.52e9 decodes are 8x above N*, so it is the one sweep in the repository that both exceeded N* and used an uncorrected fixed bar. Every other sweep with a documented trial count (B-04 6.2e6, B-05 7.1e4, R16-KDF 6.9e5, R16-PRNG 5.3e4, R12-A1 768, F-01 40) is below N*, where the -5.5 floor is the correct binding constraint. Round 17's lanes sit above N* on offsets-scanned, but the statistic they adjudicate is a maximum over ~1e3 beam decodes, so the floor is the right bar there too - see L7-C-THRESHOLD-CALIBRATION.
additional_not_covered: Round 8's score scale is not the current score_norm scale, so its best of -13.13 is not directly comparable to any bar quoted here

entries.was: NEGATIVE. 6,224,300 decodes across stages A/B/C/D, 0 over the -5.5 bar.
entries.restated_coverage: NEGATIVE for a modern-English, archaic-English or LP1-register plaintext, at measured power 1.00 (the register the Liber Primus has demonstrably used scores -4.33). Measured power of the same sweep against a Latin plaintext 0.33-0.50, against half-vowel-abbreviated English 0.25-0.33, against Welsh 0.00, against vowel-dropped English 0.00 (where the correct key scores BELOW a wrong key). Re-scoring the stored top-50 (L7-A-ARCHIVE-RESCORE) extends the negative to Latin, Old English and half-vowel English at rank-1 power; it does not extend it to Welsh or vowel-dropped English. Separately, the decoder covers only a rejection sampler that advances the key by exactly one symbol per rejection with no other source of drift (L7-B-BEAM-ENVELOPE).

rejection samplers that consume more than one draw per rejection
any independent key-drift source above ~1 event per 60 runes

entries.was: NEGATIVE. 14,522,916,046 offsets scored, ~8.4e9 effective after each lane's measured prefilter survival.
entries.restated_coverage: NEGATIVE for an English plaintext. The offsets were SELECTED by an English rune-index trigram prefilter (lib_padsweep.trigram_model, trained on the same kjv/moby/pride/war corpus) over a 24-rune head, and only the top 40 per sign were beam-escalated and adjudicated by the English quadgram beam. The measured prefilter survival (0.375-0.875, non-monotone in pad size) was measured on ENGLISH plants only, so it is not a coverage discount for a non-English plaintext - that coverage is unmeasured, neither zero nor one. Additionally the ms=8 correction R17 published covers constant key runs up to length 8, not beyond (measured: ms=8 fails at run 16 and 32 under a hard filter).
